items.e: They praised themselves in this regard: **“We saw and merited this light that was walking with us, and we still exist in the world,”** since we merited the light about which it is stated: **“For man shall not see Me and live,”** and we are alive in this world (see Tikkunei Zohar 69, p. 115b).

**112. “They walked and reached a certain etc.” They walked and reached a certain mountain, as the sun was setting. They began rattling the branches of a tree on the mountain against each other, and chanting a song. As they were walking, they heard a loud voice saying: “Holy sons of God, you who are scattered among the living in this world, you lamps of the members of the academy, gather to your places to delight with your Master in the Torah.” They became afraid and remained standing in their places, and** [then] **sat.**

Explanation: **“They walked and reached a certain mountain.”** This is the mystical meaning of the mountain about which King David declared: “Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord, and who will stand in His holy place?” (Psalms 24:3). When they climbed the mountain the sun was setting, an allusion to the departure of their lights. The branches of the trees were rattling against each other, which is the mystical meaning of the conversing of the trees. They heard a song from them, in the mystical meaning of the verse: “Then all the trees of the wood shall sing for joy” (Psalms 96:12).

**“They heard a loud voice etc.”** That is, they heard a loud voice instructing them to return to their places to delight with the Lord and His Torah, that is, that they should descend from the mountain. It called them **“holy sons of God”** due to their sublime level. However, it [also] alluded to them that the people of this world are unworthy of dwelling together with them. This is the meaning of the allusion to them, **“you who are scattered among the living in this world.”** In other words, the people of this world are unsuitable for them, since they would be unable to tolerate each other.
Accordingly, **“they became afraid,”** and yet they did not descend from the mountain but arose, sat, and did not move from their places.

**113. “In the meantime a voice sounded out etc.” Meanwhile, a voice sounded out as before, declaring: “Strong rocks, lofty hammers, behold the master of the colors, who is embroidered in images, standing on the platform** [ itztavna ]. **Come in and gather together.” At that moment they heard the sound of the branches of the trees, loud and strong, and they recited: “The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars”** (Psalms 29:5). **Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba fell on their faces, and a great fear fell upon them. They rose in haste and left, and they heard nothing. They emerged from the mountain and left. Itztavna ** means platform, since the Aramaic translation of “on the platform” (II Kings 11:14) is “on the astavna .”

Explanation: It was explained above (section #105#, last paragraph) that the reason they were unable **“to drive the donkeys,”** meaning that they were unable to raise more feminine waters, was because Rav Hamnuna Saba had already finished his task of assisting them. Consequently, the power of his donkeys was nullified, and they could not use them anymore in order to raise feminine waters and merit a higher level. Rabbi Elazar therefore stated above: **“But we did not merit to observe and further know the secrets of the wisdom.”**

The relationship between the attainment of brains and the nullification of the ability to raising feminine waters requires explanation. The idea is that once they had attained the height of yeḥida , which is the revelation of the soul of Benayahu Ben Yehoyada through Rav Hamnuna Saba, they experienced what has been explained with respect to the soul of Benayahu Ben Yehoyada. Once the partition of Ban had been nullified from them, the partition of Sag was nullified together with it. Therefore, they were unable to raise more feminine waters, and **“left the donkeys”** (section #105#, last paragraph; see there). It was explained there that the whole cessation of the illumination from the body of the Atik was in order to grant them the strength to distill the partition of Sag for themselves anew. Then the Ban would return to be Sag , at which point they would once again raise feminine waters, and would again go from strength to strength (Psalms 84:8); see there.

Now, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba as well, from when they left the donkeys and walked until here, all these exploits to that stage were enough for them to distill new strength for raising feminine waters once again and to restore the Ban back to being Sag . It thus states: **“A voice sounded out as before, declaring: Strong rocks, lofty hammers,”** since they had endured all the great trials thus far and had mustered the strength to withstand them like strong rocks. They had also prevailed over all the obstacles, until they smashed them like a great hammer descending down from a great height.

They thereby caused: **“Behold the master of the colors, who is embroidered in images, standing on the platform.”** The Bina is called “master of the colors,” since she herself is without any color at all (but is totally mercy), and yet all the colors awaken and emerge from [ Bina ]. Through their endurance like a mighty rock against all those trials, the Bina was now embroidered with images afresh. This is why the Bina is called “**the master of the colors, embroidered in images,”** since [ Bina ] received the power to be established with a partition, upon which new levels and heights, called “images,” emerge, while she is **“standing on the platform”** [ itztavna ]; itztavna meaning a throne. Now the Bina has been established in the mystical meaning of the throne, as it was before. Therefore, **“come in and gather together,”** [for] it is time for you to enter your places in the holy [path], as you were earlier.

**“At that hour they heard the sound of the branches of the trees, loud and strong, and they recited: The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars.”** In other words, together with the voice informing them that the partition of the Bina and the throne had been established, they also heard a voice from the branches of the trees declaring: “**The voice of the Lord breaks the cedars.”** This was alluding to them that all the cedars that were obstructions on their way to the holy had already been broken. **“They emerged from the mountain”** because they had now mustered the strength to exit the mountain and make their way in the holy [path] as before.

**114. “When they arrived at the house of etc.” When they arrived at the house of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Shimon, son of Lakunya, they saw Rabbi Shimon Bar Yoḥai there** and **they rejoiced** [and] **Rabbi Shimon** [also] **rejoiced. He said to them: “You must have passed through a path of miracles and lofty signs, for I have just been sleeping and I saw you and Benayahu Ben Yehoyada sending you two crowns by means of a certain old man, to crown you. Certainly, the Holy One, blessed be He, was on that path. Furthermore, I see that your faces have changed.” Rabbi Yosei said** [to them]: **“You spoke well, that a sage is preferable to a prophet.” Rabbi Elazar came and placed his head between the knees of his father, Rabbi Shimon, and related the incident to him.**

Explanation: This alludes to two matters: 1) That they had once again merited and attained the brains of Sag , which [are represented by] the aspect of the **father-in-law** of Rabbi Elazar (as stated in section #85#, above, 7th paragraph), who is called **Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Shimon, son of Lakunya.** 2) That now the Sag had connected together with the Ab for them in an unending [fusion through collision]. The father of Rabbi Elazar, who is Rabbi Shimon, alludes to the brains of [the level of] Ab . This is the meaning of the statement: **“When they arrived at the house of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Shimon, son of Lakunya, they saw Rabbi Shimon Bar Yoḥai there,”** as now they had merited the lofty level in which their [aspect of] Ban had become actual Sag again, forever, and also in an unending fusion with the [level of] Ab .

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Sending you two crowns by means of a certain old man.”** He is alluding to them that **Benayahu Ben Yehoyada** had sent to them, via Rav Hamnuna Saba, **two crowns:** 1) Brains of yeḥida , which is the aspect of **Benayahu Ben Yehoyada** himself; 2) The new brains of Ab Sag that they have now attained, which are also drawn forth through the strength of Benayahu Ben Yehoyada.

In other words, he was alluding and saying to them, “This is the continuation of the trials and exploits you experienced, through which you merited the current level, which is itself also a direct extension from the great light of [Benayahu Ben Yehoyada's] soul. Thus, Benayahu Ben Yehoyada sent them **two crowns** by means of Rav Hamnuna Saba. This is the meaning of the statement: **“Certainly, the Holy One, blessed be He, was on that path,”** that is, all those setbacks that befell you are not flaws, Heaven forfend, but rather **the Holy One, blessed be He,** Himself led you to your lofty status.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Furthermore, I see that your faces have changed.”** In addition to your attainment, I see that your faces are strongly shining, on account of **the path** on which you walked. Had there been any flaws in it, Heaven forfend, you certainly would not have merited those bright faces I can see upon you.

**“Rabbi Yosei said: You spoke well, that a sage is preferable to a prophet.”** They thought that this is why all those exploits had happened to them, [that it was] because they grew conceited in their minds over our teacher Moses. They thought about themselves: “A sage is preferable to a prophet,” as they said, **“we saw and merited this light that was walking with us, and we still exist in the world”** (see section #111#, above).” Regarding this, Rabbi Yosei comforted them: **“You spoke well, that a sage is preferable to a prophet,”** that is, your statement was sincere.

**115. “Rabbi Shimon was afraid etc.” Rabbi Shimon was afraid and wept, saying: “O Lord, I have heard the report of You and am afraid”** (Habakkuk 3:2). **Habakkuk stated this verse when he saw his death and his revival by means of Elisha. Why is he called Habakkuk? Because it is stated: “At this season, when the time comes round, you shall embrace** [ ḥoveket ] **a son”** (II Kings 4:16), **for this** Habakkuk **was the son of the Shunammite. There were two embraces: One from his mother and one from Elisha, as it is written, “And he put his mouth upon his mouth** [and his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and he stretched himself upon him, and the flesh of the child warmed]” (II Kings 4:34).

Explanation: A question arises in this context: How is it possible that through his blessing the prophet Elisha extended to the Shunammite a seed that is not sustainable? The explanation is that the prophet Elisha was greater than all the prophets apart from Moses (as stated in the Zohar , Parashat Beshallaḥ , 2). He merited the aspect of souls from the supernal Garden of Eden, [souls in which the aspect of] Ban was already in a state of complete purity and wholeness, as it will be in the future. Therefore, when [Elisha] pulled the son to [the Shunammite], he was not careful to tie him to the male world, for he told her: **“You shall embrace a son,”** and he tied that embrace only to the side of Nukba . Since the Nukba , which is the Ban , is near the kelippot and the Sitra Aḥara , the Sitra Aḥara clung to him and he died.

Thus, the cause of the death was the result of the prophet’s lofty, exalted state, since his own Ban was already cleansed of any grip of the Sitra Aḥara and death. This is why the prophet was surprised: “And the Lord hid it from me and did not tell me” (II Kings 4:27). In other words, he could not even contemplate that death could occur to [the child] as a result of [Elisha's] connection to the Ban alone. Consequently, [Elisha] had to return and revive him, and tie him to the higher world, in the mystical meaning of the resurrection of the dead, as will be explained here.

The mystical meaning of the embrace is that the essence of a child is the whiteness in it, which is from the father ( Nidda 31a), which is the mystical meaning of Ḥokhma . Ḥokhma is called “whiteness,” as is known, and this is the mystical meaning of: “In wisdom [ ḥokhma ] You have made them all” (Psalms 104:24). However, [ Ḥokhma ] requires the enclothing of the [light of giving], since there cannot be Ḥokhma without clothing of the [light of giving]. Therefore, the redness of the mother is required, which is the mystical meaning of the partition that extends the [light of giving] to enclothe the Ḥokhma . By means of the embrace of Ḥokhma by the [light of giving], the child is drawn and sustained. This is the meaning of the statement: **“For this was the son of the Shunammite,”** that is, this embrace of Ḥokhma by the [light of giving], performed on the child, was all from his mother the Shunammite, that is, only from the side of Ban .

It thus states: **“There were two embraces: One from his mother and one from Elisha.”** For when [Elisha] revived [the boy], [Elisha] drew down the whiteness and redness anew for him. Thus, Elisha made a second embrace for him, and as a result he had **two embraces, one from his mother and one from Elisha.**

**116. “I found in the book of King Solomon etc.” I found in the book of King Solomon** that Elisha **engraved on** Habakkuk **the engraved name of seventy-two names, in words,** for each word consists of three letters (as stated in the Zohar , Parashat Beshallaḥ , 173, in the last diagram; see there). **The letters of the alphabet that his father had initially engraved upon him had flown from him when he died. Now when Elisha embraced him, he carved in him all those letters of the seventy-two names. These engraved letters of those seventy-two names are two hundred and sixteen letters,** that is, three letters for each name.

Explanation: The letters from which a fetus is constructed are **216**, and they are of the aspect of the illumination of Ḥokhma that is drawn from Yisrael Sabba and Tevuna . Thus, the child is considered to contain **216** letters, which is the numerical value of ** re’iyah ** [ reish-alef-yod-heh , “vision”], meaning the light of the eyes, which is Ḥokhma . In the phase of maturity, when a garment of [the light of giving] is received from the higher world, from [ Abba and Imma Ila'in ] and 216 [letters] are enclothed in [the garments], the [fetus] is then called by the name **“seventy-two words,”** since each of their three letters join to form a single word, and they are [thus] **seventy-two words.**

When [the fetus] only has the [light of giving] for enclothing from the lower world, it is regarded as **216 letters.** But when it attains the male [aspect of the level of] Ab , that is, the [light of giving] from the higher world, all [sets of] three letters join to form single words, and that is the mystical meaning of the name ** Ab **. [The Zohar ] thus states that Elisha **“engraved on him the engraved name of seventy-two names, in words.”** For when [Elisha] revived the son of the Shunammite, who was Habakkuk, Elisha engraved on him **seventy-two words** from **216 letters.** [This was in order to] extend to [the boy] the [light of giving] from the higher world, called the male aspect of ** Ab **, which arranges the **216 letters** in rectified lines of three letters in each word. When the letters are enclothed in [the lights of giving in order to form them into words], this is the mystical meaning of the name ** Ab **, which is the brains of Ḥokhma in a completed state.

However, beforehand, while he had only the [light of giving] of the Nukba , they still lacked the [state of] combining into **seventy-two words.** That is, they contained no words, that is, no vessels for the enclothing of Ḥokhma . They were called only by the name **216 letters,** because they still could be grasped by the Sitra Aḥara . Consequently, the brains of Ḥokhma could not be enclothed there.

[The Zohar ] thus states: **“Since the letters of the alphabet etc.”** These **216 letters** that Habakkuk had from the time of his birth, **flew** and departed **from him** at the time of death, and therefore [Elisha] had to draw forth a new [set of] 216 letters and seventy-two names for him. This is why it states that **“Elisha carved all those letters in** [Habakkuk’s] **spirit, to revive him with letters of the seventy-two names”** [section #117#, below], since he had to engrave 216 letters in him anew, in order to combine the 216 letters into seventy-two words by means of the higher [light of giving], through which they became **seventy-two names.**

**117. “Elisha carved all those letters etc.” Elisha carved all those letters in** Habakkuk’s **spirit, to revive him with letters of the seventy-two names. He called him Habakkuk,** which is **a name that completes** and alludes to **all the sides,** for **it completes** and alludes to two **embraces, as stated, and it completes** and alludes to **the secret of the two hundred and sixteen letters of the holy name,** since Habakkuk has the numerical value of 216, from which the seventy-two names were formed, as stated above. **He revived and brought back his spirit with** seventy-two **names, and revived his entire body to its proper state with** 216 **letters, and therefore he is called Habakkuk.**

Explanation: [The name of] **Habakkuk** reflects the two **embraces** [ ḥibukim ], and hence [the expression] **“it completes the embraces.”** Furthermore, **Habakkuk** has the numerical value of **216,** and this is [why it states] **“completes the secret of the two hundred and sixteen letters.”** The meaning is that Ḥokhma is called **“the secret of the two hundred and sixteen letters.”** However, an embrace is required, that is, the enclothing [of Ḥokhma in] the [light of giving], as stated. Now, in the first embrace, which was from the side of **his mother**, the Ḥokhma could not yet be revealed in the **216 letters,** since the Sitra Aḥara had a hold of the redness of **his mother.** But now that **Elisha** drew forth an embrace for him from the [light of giving] of the higher world, from the Abba and Imma (father and mother), the letters combined into words, and the brains of Ḥokhma were permanently enclothed in the words, since there is no longer a purchase for the Sitra Aḥara in the [light of giving] of the higher world.

The name **Habakkuk** reflects two **embraces**, an embrace from **his mother,** and another embrace that he received, from **Elisha.** He is completed from all sides, both from Ḥokhma in its fullness, and from the [light of giving] in its fullness. This is the meaning of the statement: **“It completes the embraces, as stated, and it completes the secret of the two hundred and sixteen letters of the holy name.”** The embraces are the [light of giving] of the [ Abba and Imma Ila'in ] and **“the secret of the two hundred and sixteen,”** which is the Ḥokhma .

[The Zohar ] continues: **“He revived and brought back his spirit with** [seventy-two] **words, and revived his entire body to its proper state with** [216] **letters.”** The words that were formed from the **216 letters** were fashioned by the second embrace of **Elisha,** since [Habakkuk] was returned to life by means of this embrace. This [embrace] is the drawing forth of [the light of giving] from the higher world, where there is no purchase for the Sitra Aḥara , which is death. Through the **“secret of the two hundred and sixteen letters,”** the Ḥokhma was sustained in [the boy], meaning the existence of his entire body in its proper state, since the brains of Ḥokhma complete the body into a state of wholeness.

The following question arises: Since the **216 letters** [the boy] had from his birth **flew from him** upon death, why, then, was he called **Habakkuk,** after **the two embraces** [ ḥibukin ]? After all, his mother’s embrace flew from him upon [his] death and he was left with only **Elisha’s** embrace. The answer is that in fact, **Elisha** did not draw forth anything new for him in his revival, apart from the embrace that he drew for him from the higher mother, Sag , in which lies the mystical meaning of the resurrection of the dead. However, the **216 letters,** as well as the embrace from **his mother,** from Ban , were merely revived. They are the same 216 letters and Ban from the time of his birth, since otherwise he would have been a whole new soul, and resurrection would not be applicable to him.

Thus, he now has literally **two embraces,** since the first embrace of **his mother** has also been revived. The mystical meaning is that the Ban ascended and enclothed the Sag , and since the Ban is in the place of the Sag , the [light of giving] are of the level the higher world [of Sag ] and there is no purchase in them for the Sitra Aḥara , which is death. Consequently, he is called **Habakkuk,** after the **two embraces** [ ḥibukim ].

**118. “He said, ‘O Lord, etc.” He said: “O Lord, I have heard the report of You and am afraid”** (Habakkuk 3:2). This means: **I heard what had happened to me, that I tasted from that world,** that is, at the time of his death, before Elisha revived him, **and I became afraid. He began to request mercy for his soul, saying: “O Lord, may Your work” that You performed for me, “in the midst of the years” be “ ḥaiyaihu ”** and ḥaiyaihu is like **“his life”** [ ḥayav ]. **Whoever connects to those ancient years,** which are the sefirot of Atik , **life connects to him. “In the midst of the years make it known”** (Habakkuk 3:2), meaning to bestow life **upon that level where there is no life,** which is Malkhut of Malkhut , for “make it known” means “bestow.”

Explanation: His fear is from the past, since he has already been completed from all sides and now fear does not apply to him, except for the fear he experienced in the past, when he departed from the world. This is the meaning of his statement: **“I heard what had happened to me, that I tasted from that world,”** that is, after his death, before **Elisha** revived him. From there he draws forth fear even now, to be a partition for him to raise feminine waters. This is the meaning of **“he began to request mercy for his soul,”** that is, through the strength of the fear from the past, he began to raise feminine waters, which is the mystical meaning of the request for mercy for himself.

This is also the mystical meaning of the partition of the future, in the mystical meaning of [the stage] after the Ban returns to being Sag . At that time, it will be the stage of “He will eliminate death forever” (Isaiah 25:8), and there will be no possible power for fear, [no need to fight to] keep himself in purity and guard from any grip [of the Sitra Aḥara ]. Any aspect of fear will then be from the power of the past, since its imprints will remain in Ban even after it has become Sag . This is a necessary matter, for there is no rectification of the partition without fear. Rabbi Shimon told them this exposition on Habakkuk in connection to this mystical meaning, to teach them that they will also receive fear from this path of miracles and the lofty signs through which they passed, like Habakkuk in accordance with his level, for he made use of this fear.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“May Your work that You performed for me in the midst of the years be his life.”** He had two types of **years**: **Years** before his death and **years** after his resurrection. In between, he was deceased in the world of truth. He states regarding the time when he was in that world, which was **in the midst of** these two aspects of **years, “may Your work that You performed for me in the midst of the years be his life.”** In other words, by my remembering the period of my death which was in **the midst of the years,** I connect to the life of the higher world, through which **Elisha** revived me (as stated just above). **“I heard what had happened to me, that I tasted from that world, and I became afraid.”**

Now, the seven lower [ sefirot ] of [ Atik Yomin ] are called **“ancient years,”** and this is because of the Malkhut of Adam Kadmon which is enclothed in them. They are more **ancient** than the first constriction, like Adam Kadmon , and they do not illuminate during the 6, 000 years, but only at the completion of the rectification. The seven lower [ sefirot ] of [ Atik Yomin ] illuminate in the 6, 000 years [only] with respect to the [process of] rectifying the second constriction, in the mystical meaning of the small [letter] heh of hibare’am [“when they were created”], as is known.

However, the death of **Habakkuk** completely purified him, like at the completion of the rectification, and therefore he merited to connect to those earlier years of [ Atik Yomin ] through the strength of the embrace and the resurrection of the dead which he merited by means of **Elisha.** This is the meaning of: **“Your work that You performed for me in the midst of the years,”** that is, the purity and fear that he merited **in the midst of the years**, the period of his death. **“Be his life,”** that by the strength of this fear he will merit to connect to those earlier years of [ Atik Yomin ], that life which is an eternal life. [the Zohar ] thus states: **“Whoever connects to those earlier years, life connects to him,”** for life connects to him forever.

This is the meaning of the statement: **“In the midst of the years make it known, upon that level where there is no life at all.”** Through the purity that he merited on account of his death, the Ban received its complete rectification, since it ascended and became Sag upon his death, as stated. Then it was in that level where there is no life at all, which is Malkhut of Malkhut , [a level] that lacks any [fusion through collision] prior to the completion of the rectification (as stated in section #43#, above, 5th paragraph). [Following this rectification of Ban ], this level [of Malkhut of Malkhut ] now also receives its life [and undergoes fusions].

**119. “Rabbi Shimon wept, etc.” Rabbi Shimon wept and said: “I, too, was afraid of the Holy One, blessed be He, from what I heard.” He placed his hands upon his head and declared: “Now, Rav Hamnuna Saba is the light of the Torah; you merited to see him face-to-face, and I did not merit** [to see] **him.” He fell upon his face and saw him uprooting mountains** and **lighting candles in the chamber of the King Messiah.** [Rav Hamnuna Saba] **said to him, “My rabbi, in that world you will be alongside the heads of the academies, before the Holy One, blessed be He.” From that day onwards he would call his son Rabbi Elazar, and Rabbi Abba, Peniel** [“face of God”], **as it is stated:** “[And Jacob called the name of the place Peniel], **for I have seen God face-to-face”** (Genesis 32:31).

Explanation: He praised himself that he too had made use of that same fear of the prophet Habakkuk, that is, **from what he heard**, from the time of the past, in the mystical meaning of the verse: **“I have heard the report of You and am afraid”** (Habakkuk 3:2, as stated just above, in the beginning of section #118#).

Now, in the chamber of the King Messiah, all the rectifications that must be revealed at the completion of the rectification, upon the arrival of King Messiah, are already prepared and ready. Not a single tiny detail is missing. Those souls that are in the chamber of the King Messiah are all those who have already merited the completion of the rectification, from the root of their own souls.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And saw him uprooting mountains** and **lighting candles in the chamber of the King Messiah.” Rav Hamnuna Saba** is the master of these rectifications in the chamber of the Messiah. He **uproots the mountains** of the Sitra Aḥara , in the mystical meaning of the appearance [of the Sitra Aḥara ] to the righteous as a tall mountain ( Sukka 52a), and he **lights candles**, that is, he establishes the new partition with respect to the Sag to allow the raising of feminine waters at the completion of the rectification. The mystical meaning of the feminine waters is called “lights of fire,” and that is the mystical meaning of: “The soul of man is the candle of the Lord” (Proverbs 20:27). This is because the light of the sun is indicative of the downward flow of the masculine waters, like the light of the sun descending to us from above to below. The light of fire is the mystical meaning of the returning light, which ascends from below to above, like a flame rising from a candle.

[The Zohar ] thus states that these two rectifications, to remove the Sitra Aḥara , and to raise and light the candles **in the chamber of the King Messiah,** are in the hands **of Rav Hamnuna Saba.** Those completely righteous ones who require these two rectifications merit them only through the revelation of the soul **of Rav Hamnuna Saba.** [Rav Hamnuna Saba] informed [Rabbi Shimon] that he and his disciples, Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Abba, would also merit to serve in the chamber of the King Messiah after their deaths, and that they would be alongside him there, and be **heads of academies** there **before the Holy One, blessed be He.**

**120. “ Bereshit . Rabbi Ḥiyya, etc.”  Bereshit . Rabbi Ḥiyya opened** [his discourse by citing this verse]: **“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; all those who practice it will have a good understanding; His praise endures forever”** (Psalms 111:10). **“The beginning of wisdom” –** the question is raised: **This verse should have stated: “The fear of the Lord is the end of wisdom,” since the fear of the Lord** is the mystical meaning of Malkhut , **which is the end of wisdom** [ Ḥokhma ] The answer is: **Rather,** Malkhut **is the first to enter the level of the supernal Ḥokhma , as it is stated: “Open for me the gates of righteousness** [ tzedek ]” (Psalms 118:19), which are the gates of Malkhut , called tzedek . **“This is the gate of the Lord”** (Psalms 118:20) **– certainly, if one does not enter through this gate, he will never enter to the supernal King, for He is lofty, hidden, and concealed, and He fashioned gates for Himself, one above the other.**

Explanation: The question being asked is: Since the **fear of the Lord** is the sefira of Malkhut , which is at the end of the ten sefirot , [the verse] should have stated: **“The fear of the Lord is the end of wisdom.”** [The Zohar ] then states: **“The supernal King** […] **is lofty, hidden, and concealed** etc.” This is not a metaphor but the point itself. It means that since He is a lofty, hidden, and concealed King, and no thought can grasp Him at all, He therefore fashioned many gates **one above the other,** by virtue of which [He] made the approach to Him possible. This is the mystical meaning of the verse: “Open for me the gates of righteousness.” These are the gates that God has fashioned and [thereby] provided the option for the righteous to approach Him via those gates.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And at the end of all the gates, He made one gate with several locks** etc.” [section #121#, below]. This is the gate called Malkhut of Malkhut , which is the end point of all the supernal gates. This last gate is the first gate to the **supernal Ḥokhma .** In other words, it is only possible to merit the supernal Ḥokhma specifically after the attainment of this last gate, because this [gate] is the first gate for attaining the s**upernal Ḥokhma **. With regard to this mystical meaning, it is stated: **“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom,”** since it is specifically “the fear of the Lord” [which is Malkhut ] that is the last gate, which is the first [gate] to [reach] the Ḥokhma of the Lord.

**121. “And at the end of all the gates, etc.” And at the end of all the gates, He made one gate with several locks, with several openings, with several chambers, one above the other. He declared: “Anyone who wishes to enter My** [Presence], **this gate will be the first to Me. One who enters, will enter through this gate.” Here too, the first gate to the supernal Ḥokhma is the fear of the Lord,** which is Malkhut , **and this is** the one called **“first.”**

Explanation: It is necessary to understand thoroughly the meaning of **“locks,” “openings,”** and **“chambers.”** Know that these are three forms that come one after the other, with respect to a single substance. This is a very profound matter and I will make the effort to explain as best as I can, so that these words of the Zohar will be somewhat comprehensible. One should know that although it is clear that no thought can grasp Him in any manner at all, the truth is that [God’s] intent in [creating] Creation was to provide pleasure to His creatures. Now, no pleasure can be grasped by a created being if [that being] is necessarily separate from the Creator, Heaven forbid. Furthermore, the Sages have stated that the Holy One, blessed be He, yearned to dwell in the lower realms.

The common denominator for understanding those two contradicting concepts is that the world was created as the exact opposite of God, [opposite as] the two extremes [on a spectrum], with regard to every single point. This world was created out of the aspect of the will to receive, which is the form that is opposite to God, since He does not have even a shred of this will. This is the mystical meaning of: “A man is born a man as a wild donkey’s colt” (Job 11:12). From this perspective, all matters of the guidance of His Providence in this world are in absolute contradiction to [His] intent for the Creation, which is only to provide pleasure to His creatures, [pleasure] that is correlated with the will to receive within us, which is our taste and our standard of measurement.

This is the mystical meaning of the **locks** on the gates. For in truth, all the many contradictions to His unity, which we experience in this world, although they initially separate us from God, when we make the effort to fulfill the Torah and mitzvot with love, with our souls and our might, as we are commanded (that is, in order to provide satisfaction to our Maker), then all those forces of separation do not affect us into diminishing any of the love of God with all our souls and might. [Then] each and every contradiction that we have overcome subsequently becomes a gate for the attainment of His wisdom. Every contradiction contains a special quality, which reveals a unique level in the attainment of Him. Those worthy individuals who have merited this, will transform darkness into light and bitter into sweet. All the powers of separation, including both the darkness of the intellect and the bitterness of the body, have for [such people] become gates for the attainment of lofty levels. The darkness thus turns into a great light, and the bitter becomes sweet.

[This conversion of darkness to light takes place such that] to the degree that all the workings of His Providence had previously been [experienced as] forces of separation for [such people], [these workings] have now all transformed for [such people] into forces of unification. They have thus tilted the entire world to the scale of merit, for each and every force now serves for them as **gates of righteousness,** through which they will enter to receive from God everything that He has thought with regard to them, to provide them with pleasure, in [His initial] intent for the Creation, and [hence the verse]: “This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it” (Psalms 118:20).

However, before meriting to transform the will to receive that is within us, through the Torah and commandments, into “receiving in order to give,” there are powerful locks on those gates to the Lord, since at that stage they have the opposite task, which is to drive us away from God. This is why these forces of separation are called **“locks,”** because they block the gates of approach and distance us from God. However, if we overcome them, such that they do not affect us by cooling His love from our hearts, the **locks** then become **openings,** the darkness becomes light, and the bitter becomes sweet, as stated. The reason is that for each and every lock we receive a special level of His Providence, and they become **openings,** levels of attainment of Him. These levels we receive from these **openings** subsequently become **chambers** of the Ḥokhma .

This is how the **locks, openings,** and **chambers** are three forms that affect our single substance, that is, the will to receive that is within us. Before we transform it into “receiving in order to give” satisfaction to our Maker, this substance transforms, in accordance with our taste, the light into darkness and the sweet into bitter, since all the workings of His Providence drive us from Him. At that time, **locks** are fashioned from the will to receive in us, but after our repentance, when we merit [the level of] “receiving in order to give,” all the **locks** become **openings,** and then the **openings** become **chambers,** as explained. This must be kept in mind for all that follows, for I will not restate these ideas.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Anyone who wishes to enter My** [Presence], **this gate will be the first to Me.”** The meaning of the gates has already been thoroughly explained; see above. **“The end of all the gates”** refers to the last aspect within them, the lowliest of all, which can be called Malkhut of Malkhut . [The Zohar ] is saying that in order to merit the **supernal Ḥokhma **, this gate, the last of all of them, becomes the first gate to the chamber of the **supernal Ḥokhma **. For in truth, all the gates serve as **openings** and **chambers** to the Ḥokhma of the Lord, but it is impossible to attain the **supernal Ḥokhma ** without attaining the last gate specifically, since it is the first [gate] for the s**upernal Ḥokhma **.

This is the meaning of the statement: **“And this is** [the one called] **“first** [ reishit ],” which is referring to [the word] ** Bereshit ,** with which the Torah begins. ** Bereshit ** represents the fear of God from the aspect of the last gate, which is the **first** [gate] for attaining the s**upernal Ḥokhma **.

**122. “ Bet , these two, etc.”** [The letter] ** bet from Bereshit ** indicates **that these two combine together** in Malkhut . **They are two points, one is concealed and hidden, and** [the other] **one is in a revealed state. Since there is no separation between them, they are called “first,”** that is, only **one and not two.** For **one who takes this** one, **takes that** one as well, **and all is one, for He and His name are one, as it is stated: “That they may know that it is You alone whose name is YHVH”** (Psalms 83:19).

Explanation: Those two points are the mystical meaning of the tempering of the attribute of judgment with the attribute of mercy, when Malkhut ascended and was tempered in Bina , which is the attribute of mercy, in the mystical meaning of the verse: “So they both walked” (Ruth 1:19), which is the mystical meaning of Bina and Malkhut together (as stated in the Zohar , Parashat Pineḥas , 57, and in several other places). Thus, the partition that was established upon Malkhut consists of both [ Malkhut and Bina ], and therefore there are **two points** combined as one there. [The Zohar ] continues, that **“one is concealed and hidden, and** [the other] **one is in a revealed state,”** because the aspect of judgment in the point of Malkhut is **concealed and hidden,** and only the aspect of mercy from the point of Bina **is in a revealed state.** If not [for this concealment] the world would not be able to exist, as the Sages state: “Initially, the world was created with the attribute of judgment; He saw that the world could not exist, and partnered the attribute of mercy with it” ( Bereshit Rabba , 1).

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Since there is no separation between them, they are called ‘first, ’ one and not two. One who takes this, takes that.”** In other words, although the attribute of judgment is **concealed,** this does not mean that the [fusion through collision] is not performed upon it, for those two points have become literally one, and the point of the Malkhut also receives this fusion with the point of Bina , only secretly rather than **in a revealed state.** The name reishit [“first”], which is in a singular [as opposed to plural] form, indicates this, that they are both one.

**“And all is one, for He and His name are one.” “He”** refers to the Bina , while **“His name”** refers to the Malkhut . The text is saying that in the mystical meaning of **“He and His name are one”** both of them must necessarily be one, since when they are one the Malkhut also receives the supernal [fusion through collision] together with the Bina . In this [manner], the attribute of judgment is also ultimately tempered by itself at the completion of the rectification, when “on that day, the Lord shall be one and His name one” (Zechariah 14:9).

On account of this attribute of judgment, which is incorporated in the ** bet ** of Bereshit , [the attribute of judgment, Malkhut , ] is called the “first” towards the Ḥokhma . The rectification [of the attribute of judgment] will be at the completion of the rectification, at which time the s**upernal Ḥokhma ** will be revealed, and “the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord” (Isaiah 11:9), since it is the last gate, which is the first gate to the Ḥokhma . This is why it cites the verse: **“That they may know** that it is You [alone] whose name is the Lord,” for then the knowledge will be revealed the throughout the earth.

**123. “Why is it called the fear, etc.” Why is** the Malkhut **called “the fear of the Lord”?** He answers: **Because** the Malkhut **is the tree of good and evil. If a person merits, it is good; if he does not merit, it is evil. Therefore, fear resides in that place. It is the gateway to reach all the good that is in the world. “A good understanding”** (Psalms 111:10) **is those two gates,** that is, the two points, **which are as one. Rabbi Yosei said: “A good understanding” – this is the tree of life, which is a good understanding without any evil at all. Since no evil resides in it, it is a good understanding, without evil.**

Explanation: The purpose here is to explain why the last gate is called “**the fear of the Lord,”** regarding which it is stated: **“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom”** (Psalms 111:10). [The reason] is that this is the mystical meaning of the tree of knowledge with which Adam the first [man] sinned. It is due to this point [of Malkhut that is the tree] that he was punished with death, and the great fear is not to impair [this point of Malkhut ]. At the completion of the rectification, when this point will be entirely rectified in full completion, the verse: **“He will eliminate death forever”** (Isaiah 25:8) will be fulfilled. This is why it is called **“the fear of** [the Lord],” and this is the meaning of the statement: **“Therefore, fear resides in that place.”**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“it is the gateway to reach all the good that is in the world.”** The revelation of the s**upernal Ḥokhma ** is all the good of the world, which is included in [God’s initial] intent for the Creation. Since **“the fear of the Lord”** is the first gate to the s**upernal Ḥokhma **, it is thus the gate **to all the good that is in the world.**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“‘A good understanding’ is those two gates, which are as one,”** that is, the **two points** together, when they are incorporated in the ** bet ** of Bereshit . The reason why it does not state **two points,** but rather **two gates,** is that it is referring to after the rectification of the Ban [after the completion of the rectification]. At this stage these **two points** are called **two gates,** because then they are both good, without any evil at all, and therefore the verse **“a good understanding”** is possible. This is not the case before the completion of the rectification, for then they are called “the tree of knowledge of **good and evil,”** as stated.

**“Rabbi Yosei said** etc.” Rabbi Yosei does not disagree with Rabbi Ḥiyya; they merely expound the text in a different manner. Rabbi Ḥiyya explains the verse as referring to [the period after] the rectification of the Ban , when the two points become two gates, as stated, and they do not contain **evil,** but are **a good understanding without any evil at all.** Rabbi Yosei [by contrast] interprets the verse as referring to [the stage] before the completion of the rectification, when [the two points] are of the aspect of the tree of knowledge of **good and evil.** He thus states that **“a good understanding” is the tree of life,** which is Ze’er Anpin with the brains of the Imma (mother), called **“the tree of life”** because it is all good, without any evil at all, even before the completion of the rectification. That is not the case for the **two points,** which are of the aspect of **good and evil** before the completion of the rectification, and on account of which the Malkhut is called the tree of good and evil, as stated.

**124. “All those who practice it, these are etc.” “All those who practice it** [ oseihem ]**”** (Psalms 111:10). **These are “the faithful mercies of David”** (Isaiah 55:3), **the preservers of the Torah. Those who preserve the Torah are as if they are the ones who fashion** [ osim ] **it. All those who engage in Torah do not practice** [it] **while they are engaged in it, but those who preserve** it **do practice** [it], **and through this strength the verse: “His praise endures forever”** is fulfilled, **and the throne stands properly established.**

Explanation: It was explained above that this gate of the fear of the Lord, which is the last gate, is the first gate to the supernal Ḥokhma . Thus, [with respect to] **those who engage in Torah,** who have already rectified the last gate and for whom the two points have become two gates (which are “a good understanding” without evil), it is considered that **“those who engage in Torah do not practice** [it],” which is [referring to] the aspect of the **tree of the knowledge of good and evil.** However, those who have not yet merited the completion of the rectification, who are called **“preservers of the Torah,” do practice** [it], which is **good and evil,** since they have not yet rectified the sin of the tree of knowledge.

[The Zohar ] thus states that **“those who preserve the Torah are as if they are the ones who fashion it.”** It was explained above at length how all these forces of separation are transformed and become gates, and each lock becomes an opening, and every opening a chamber of Ḥokhma . Through these [openings] all the lofty levels that were incorporated in [God’s initial] intent for the Creation, which is to provide pleasure to His creatures, come forth and are revealed. See there [in greater detail].

Thus, all the wisdom and the whole Torah are fully revealed only by means of **those who preserve the Torah, who practice** [it], that is, in whom there is good and evil. This is why they are called **“preservers of the Torah,”** since it is revealed only through them. The verse calls them **“those who practice it** [ oseihem ]**,”** since it is as if they fashion [ osim ] the Torah. Were it not for their concealments, which turn into gates through their prevailing over them, the Torah would not be revealed. This is the meaning of **“those who preserve the Torah are as if they are the ones who fashion it,”** that is, they are considered **as if** they fashioned it since they reveal it.

That which [the Zohar ] states “as if” is because the Torah preceded the world ( Pesaḥim 54a), and it is certainly the case that the Holy One, blessed be He, fashioned it. However, since, without the good deeds of the “**preservers of the Torah,”** the Torah would not have been revealed, they are considered to have fashioned and made the Torah.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“Through this strength the verse: ‘His praise endures forever’** [is fulfilled].” That is, **through the strength** of **those who preserve the Torah, “His praise,”** which is all of Ḥokhma and all of Torah, **“endures forever.” [**The expression] “forever” serves to include [the stage] after the completion of the rectification. Even then, [people] will require **“the fear of the Lord,”** and after the rectification of the tree of knowledge [people] will have nowhere from which to take **“the fear of the Lord”** other than from time past, which is from the **“preservers of the Torah”** (see section #118#, above). [The preservers of the Torah] thus establish the praise of the Lord forever and ever. [The Zohar ] therefore states: **“And the throne stands properly established,”** since in this manner the **throne** will be **established properly,** for all eternity.

**125. “Rabbi Shimon was etc.” Rabbi Shimon was sitting and engaging in the Torah on the night when the bride,** which is Malkhut , **bonds with her husband. For we learned: All the colleagues, who are the members of the bridal chamber, are needed on that night, because on the day after** which is the day of Shavuot, [when] **the bride is meant to be with her husband under the wedding canopy,** [so the colleagues] **must be with her all that night and rejoice with her in her rectifications which she undergoes,** that is, **to engage in the Torah, from the Torah to the Prophets, and from the Prophets to the Writings, and in the expositions of the verses, and in the secrets of the wisdom. These are her rectifications and adornments. And she,** the bride, **and her maidens, come and stand on their heads, and she is rectified through them and rejoices in them all throughout that entire night. On the next day,** the day of Shavuot, **she comes to the wedding canopy only with them. And these** colleagues, who engage in the Torah all night long, **are called “members of the wedding canopy.” And once she comes to the wedding canopy, the Holy One, blessed be He, inquires about them, blesses them, and crowns them with the crowns of the bride. Happy is their portion.**

Explanation: There are two complementary meanings to this section: 1) The days of the exile are called **“night,”** since this is the time of the concealment of His face from the children of Israel. All the powers of separation rule over the servants of God, and yet, it is precisely at that time that the bride bonds with her husband. [This occurs] through the Torah and commandments of the righteous, who at that time are called **“the preservers of the Torah.”** All the lofty levels that are called “the secrets of the Torah” are revealed through them, since this is why they are called **“those who practice it** [ oseihem ]” (Psalms 111:10), because it is **as if** they fashion [ osim ] the Torah (see section #124#, above). Thus, the period of the exile is called **night,** “**when the bride bonds with her husband”** and **“all the colleagues, who are the members of the bridal chamber,”** are the **“preservers of the Torah.”**

The [period following the] **completion of the rectification** and the full redemption is the mystical meaning of the verse: “And there shall be one day which shall be known as the Lord’s, not day and not night; but it shall come to pass that at evening time there shall be light” (Zechariah 14:7). This is the meaning of the statement that **“on the day after, the bride is meant to be with her husband under the wedding canopy,”** for then the Ban will return to be Sag , and the Mah will be Ab , and Ab is considered to be **the day after** and a new wedding canopy.

The righteous at that time are called **“members of the wedding canopy,”** which is the mystical meaning of **those who engage in Torah,** in whom there is no **practice** [ assiya ], for [regarding that time] it is stated: “And the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord” (Isaiah 11:9). Since those righteous ones, through their good deeds, raise the Ban to be Sag , by the force of their drawing on the fear from time past, they are considered as though they fashioned this new wedding canopy, and this is why they are called **“members of the wedding canopy.”**

2) [The second explanation is]: The night of Shavuot is called **“the night when the bride bonds with her husband.”** This is because **“on the day after,** [the bride] **is meant to be with her husband under the wedding canopy,”** that is, on the day of Shavuot, the day of the receiving of the Torah. Yet this is the very same idea as the first explanation, because on the day of the receiving of the Torah there was an aspect of the completion of the rectification, in the mystical meaning of: “He will eliminate death forever and the Lord God will wipe tears from all faces” (Isaiah 25:8). This is as the Sages expounded with regard to the verse: “Graven [ ḥarut ] upon the tablets” (Exodus 32:16): Do not read ḥarut but ḥeirut [“freedom”], since freedom from the angel of death has arrived ( Shemot Rabba , 41).

However, on account of the sin of the calf they once again corrupted the rectification. Thus, the day of the receiving of the Torah is the same concept as the completion of the rectification. Accordingly, on the night before the receiving of the Torah, all the fusions of the days of concealment came to an end. This is why that night is considered **“the night when the bride bonds with her husband,”** and **“on the day after, the bride is meant to be with her husband under the wedding canopy.”** This was the festival of Shavuot, when the rectification was completed by means of freedom from the angel of death, which is the time when the righteous, through their good deeds, fashion a new wedding canopy for the bride.

Now, it will be easier for me to continue my commentary by following the first explanation. One who can analyze matters on his own will be able to transfer the concepts to the day of Shavuot [which is the second explanation], since it is the same idea.

Thus, **“all the colleagues...**” those who **preserve the Torah,** who are called **“members of the wedding canopy”** (as stated just above), must cleave to the holy Divine Presence, which is called the **bride, “throughout that entire night”** of the exile. Then, during the period of the exile, [the bride, the Divine Presence] is rectified by means of those who **preserve the Torah** through all those good deeds and Torah and mitzvot that they perform, until her purification from good and evil. She is then available for those who **engage in the Torah,** in whom there is nothing at all in the form of **practice,** but rather she is entirely **good without evil** (as stated in section #123#, above, 4th paragraph).

Therefore, all the **preservers of the Torah,** who are **“members of the bridal chamber,”** must rejoice with her over the great rectification achieved through them for the bride. [The Zohar ] thus states: **“And rejoice with her in her rectifications which she undergoes, to engage in the Torah,”** that is, in the rectifications that come before us, **“from the Torah to the Prophets...**” which must be performed with joy.

It has thus been explained that all the levels and revelations of the secrets of Torah, which are the construction of the Divine Presence for its complete rectification, are attained only by means of those who **preserve the Torah** during the exile. Consequently, all these heights and levels that emerge during the exile are called the **rectifications** of the bride and her **adornments.** These are [what are] then spelled out in detail: **“From the Torah to the Prophets** etc.” For Ḥesed , Gevura , and Tiferet are the mystical meaning of Torah; Netzaḥ and Hod are the mystical meaning of the **Prophets;** the Malkhut itself is the mystical meaning of the **Writings;** the brains of the six extremities that are drawn forth to [the bride] are the **expositions of the verses;** and the brains of the first three [ sefirot ] that are drawn forth to [the bride] are the **secrets of the wisdom.** For all these rectifications must be extended to the bride **on that night,** since the bride is completed through them for the completion of the rectification, which is the mystical meaning of the day of the wedding canopy.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“And she and her maidens** etc.” The angels in which the vessels of the “back of Malkhut of the first state” are enclothed are called “maidens that serve the Divine Presence.” [The Zohar ] adds that the Divine Presence **“stand on their heads,” of those who preserve the Torah,** in the mystical meaning of: “And above my head the Divine Presence of God.”

Together with her are the **maidens** that serve her, and she rejoices with them while she is increasingly rectified through them. [The Zohar ] thus states that she **“rejoices in them all throughout that entire night,”** that is, throughout the whole period of rectifications, which is called **“night”** (see the Zohar Ḥadash , Shir HaShirim , 159). **“On the next day**...” that is, on the day of the completion of the rectification, which is **the day of the wedding canopy,** she will be able to enter the wedding canopy only with **those who preserve the Torah,** who built and established it as much as was necessary, **from the Torah to the Prophets** etc.” This is why they are called **“members of the wedding canopy.”**

This is the meaning of the statement: **“And once she comes** [to the wedding canopy] etc.” It is known that the completion of the rectification will not bring with it anything new. Rather, by virtue of the supernal light of the Atik Yomin , all the feminine waters and masculine waters, and all the fusions and levels that emerged during the 6, 000 years one after another, will be gathered into a single fusion and one **great and precious** height, and everything will thereby be rectified (as stated in section #91#, above, 8th paragraph). Then the bride will enter the wedding canopy.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“the Holy One, blessed be He, inquires about them,”** that is, about each and every one of those who ever raised feminine waters for a supernal [fusion through collision], for it is as if He is sitting and waiting for all of them to assemble. He thus inquires and waits for each and every one of them. After they have assembled, the fusion of **“who had done mighty deeds, of Kabzeel”** is performed, as stated above (section #103#), and He **“blesses them and crowns them,”** that is, they are all blessed and crowned simultaneously. Then the rectification called **“the crowns of the bride”** is complete.

**126. “Rabbi Shimon etc.” Rabbi Shimon and all the colleagues were singing the song of the Torah. Each of them was innovating words of Torah, and Rabbi Shimon was joyful, and** so were **the rest of the colleagues. Rabbi Shimon said to them: “My sons, happy is your portion, since tomorrow the bride will come to the wedding canopy only with you, since all those who are performing the rectifications of the bride on this night and are rejoicing in her will all be recorded and written in the book of remembrance. And the Holy One, blessed be He, will bless them with seventy blessings and crowns from the higher world.”**

Explanation: The “book of remembrance” is mentioned in Malachi chapter 3, where it is stated: “You have said, it is vain to serve God… they who work wickedness are built up; they also try God, and are delivered. Then those who feared the Lord spoke one with another, and the Lord listened and heard, and a book of remembrance was written before Him, for those who feared the Lord and who thought upon His name. And they shall be Mine, says the Lord of hosts, on the day when I make a treasure etc.” (Malachi 3:14–17). These verses require explanation. At that time, they spoke to one another and uttered such contemptible observations among themselves, that “it is vain to serve God, and what profit is it that we have kept His charge...” and yet the prophet says about them: “Then those who feared the Lord spoke with one another,” and what is more, they are written in the book of remembrance before Him, “for those who feared the Lord, and who thought upon His name.”

The meaning is that at the time of the end, when the great fusion of the Atik Yomin is revealed, in the mystical meaning of **“who had done mighty deeds, of Kabzeel”** [mentioned in the previous sections], a great light will be revealed in all the levels, by means of which all flesh shall return in complete repentance out of love. There is a well-known statement of the Sages that if one merits to repent out of love, his willful transgressions become for him like merits ( Yoma 86b). This is the meaning of the prophet’s statement about those wicked ones who cursed and blasphemed amongst themselves, saying: “It is vain to serve God, and what profit is it that we have kept His charge.” On the great day of the completion of the rectification, when the light of repentance out of love will appear, even these willful transgressions, which are the worst of all, will become merits, and those who issued them will be regarded as “those who feared the Lord.”

This will happen at the completion of the rectification, as the prophet concludes: “They shall be Mine, says the Lord of hosts, on the day when I make a treasure, ’” which is on the day of the completion of the rectification. Therefore, there is necessarily a book of remembrance before Him, for the willful transgressions and iniquities that are performed in the world, since He will require them on the day when He makes a treasure, for then they will become merits and will join and complete the height of light of the completion of the rectification.

This is the meaning of the verses: “And a book of remembrance was written before Him, for those who feared the Lord, and who thought upon His name. And they shall be Mine, says the Lord of hosts, on the day when I make a treasure,” since [God] will need them then, in order to complete the height. This is why the prophet concludes: “And I will spare them, like a man spares his own son who serves him” (Malachi 3:17), for then they will be precious to [God] and dear to [Him] as though they were among those who serve [Him].

When [the Zohar ] states [that they] **“will all be recorded and written in the book of remembrance,”** this comes to include even the willful transgressions that they performed, which will then **be recorded and written** in the book of remembrance. The Holy One, blessed be He, will write them down as though they were merits, and as though they served Him through them, as the prophet states.

Now, the number seventy alludes to the brains of Ḥokhma and the first three [ sefirot ], which are called **“crowns.”** The mystical meaning of the **“blessing”** refers to the light of giving (as stated in section #37#, above). The world was created with [the letter] ** bet **, which is the mystical meaning of berakha [“blessing”], which is: “The world is built through mercy [giving]” (Psalms 89:3); study that section carefully. This aspect is of the six extremities. [The Zohar ] further states that at the completion of the rectification, the light of giving will also be an expression of **seventy crowns,** like the Ḥokhma , since the Mah and Ban will ascend to Ab Sag . This is the meaning of the statement: **“And the Holy One, blessed be He, will bless them with seventy blessings and crowns from the higher world”** of Ab Sag . Accordingly, at that time as well, the **blessings** are of the aspect of the number **seventy.**

**127. “Rabbi Shimon etc.” Rabbi Shimon opened** [his discourse] **and said: “The heavens declare the glory of God,** [and the firmament shows His handiwork” (Psalms 19:2)]. **I have already established this verse, but at this time, when the bride is awakening to enter the wedding canopy, for tomorrow, she is rectified and illuminates in her adornments with the colleagues, who rejoiced with her throughout that entire night, and she is joyous with them.**

**128. “On the next day, several etc.” On the next day, several multitudes, armies and camps, gather to her, and she and all of them,** all these armies and camps, **wait for each and every one of those who rectified her** through their Torah engagement **during this night. Once** Ze’er Anpin and Malkhut **join together and she,** the Malkhut , **sees her husband,** Ze’er Anpin , **what is written? “The heavens declare the glory of God.” “The heavens” is the bridegroom entering the wedding canopy,** and this is Ze’er Anpin , who is called “heavens.” **“Declare”** means that **they illuminate like the brightness of the sapphire, which illuminates and shines from one end of the world to the other.**

Explanation: The day of the completion of the rectification is called “tomorrow,” as the Sages have stated: “Today [is the time] to do them; tomorrow [is the time] to receive their reward” ( Eiruvin 22a). The **multitudes** are the nations of the land that do not serve God. The **armies** are the servants of God, while the **camps** refer to the supernal camps, which are the angels that accompany the souls, in the mystical meaning of the verse: “For He will give His angels charge over you, to guard you in all your ways etc.” (Psalms 91:11). The statement that **“she and all of them wait for each and every one of those”** has already been explained (section #125#, above, after the comment “Now, it will be easier for me”; see there). Just as the Holy One, blessed be He, inquires about each and every one, the Divine Presence likewise waits for each one of them.

This is why it is stated that **“once they join together and she sees her husband** etc.” She cannot see her husband until they have all gathered together, as stated [She and her husband] are dependent on one another.

**“‘The heavens’ is the bridegroom entering the wedding canopy.”** This is expounded in reference to the completion of the rectification, about which it is stated: “And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun etc.” (Isaiah 30:26). [The Zohar ] states that **“the heavens’ is the bridegroom entering the wedding canopy”** because the Holy One, blessed be He, is called **“heavens,”** and at the time of the completion of the rectification He is called a **“groom,”** in the mystical meaning of the verse: “And as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall Your God rejoice over You” (Isaiah 62:5). The meaning is that wherever it is stated: “And the Lord descended,” this involves judgment or restraint, because it is indicative of a descent from His height and exaltedness, since “strength and gladness are in His place” (I Chronicles 16:27).

However, at the completion of the rectification, when all the flaws and sins will be transformed into merits, because at that time it will become clear that all the descents were nothing other than ascents, the Holy One, blessed be He, will be called a **“groom,”** and the Divine Presence will be called a **“bride.”** The term kalah [“bride”] is related to the completion of the rectification, as in the phrase: “And it came to pass on the day that Moses had made an end [ kalot ] of setting up the Tabernacle” (Numbers 7:1), which means that he had completed all the work and construction of the Tabernacle. The word ḥatan [groom] also indicates descent, since red [“descend”] is translated [to Aramaic] as ḥut , as in the statement of the Sages: “Descend [ neḥeit ] a level to marry a woman” ( Yevamot 63a). However, this descent is greater than all the previous ascents, for it is towards the bride, which is the Divine Presence at the time of the complete rectification, when she is called a **“bride.”**

The **“wedding canopy”** is the gathering and assembling of all the returning light that emerged by means of the feminine waters that the righteous raised in all those fusions of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Divine Presence, which were revealed one after the other throughout all the days and times of the 6, 000 years [that make up the time of this world]. [Through this process] they have now all become one great, single light of returning light that ascends and hovers over the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Divine Presence, which are now called **“groom and bride.”** The returning light hovers over them like a **wedding canopy,** for which reason the righteous are then called “members of the wedding canopy.” Each and every one of them has a portion in this wedding canopy, according to the measure of the feminine waters that each raised to the partition in Makhut for raising returning light. When it states that **“the heavens’ is the bridegroom entering the wedding canopy,”** this is referring to the time of the completion of the rectification, when the Holy One, blessed be He, will be called a **“groom,”** and He will then enter His wedding canopy.

[The Zohar ] continues: **“declare”** means that **“they illuminate** etc.” **“Declare** [ mesaprim , which is similar to the language of “ sappir,” sapphire]**”** is the mystical meaning of the great [fusion through collision] that will occur in the future, as in the phrase: “A wife converses [ mesapperet ] with her husband” ( Berakhot 3a). “Sapphire [ sappir ]” is the name of the holy Divine Presence, as in the verse: “And there was under His feet the like of a paved work of sapphire stone” (Exodus 24:10). **“The brightness of the sapphire”** is the returning light that [ Malkhut ] raises from below upwards. “Illuminates” refers to the direct light, while “shines” refers to returning light. [The Zohar ] thus states that through this great fusion that will be performed at the completion of the rectification, which is a gathering together of all the fusions, the direct light and the returning light in this fusion will illuminate and shine from “one end of the world to the other,” which is the mystical meaning of: **“The heavens declare.”**

**129. “The glory of God is” etc.” “The glory of God** [ El ]” **is the glory of the bride,** that is, the Malkhut , **who is called El , as it is stated: “God** [ El ] **is furious every day”** (Psalms 7:12). **On all the days of the year she is called El , but now,** on the festival of Shavuot, **when she has** already **entered the wedding canopy, she is called “glory” and she is** [also] **called “ El .”** This is indicative of **honor on top of honor, light on top of light, and reign on top of reign.**

Explanation: The name ** El ** is the name of the great Ḥesed . Now, the verse states that “God [ El ] is furious every day,” which appears to be the opposite of Ḥesed . The concept here is that this is the mystical meaning of: “And there was evening and there was morning, one day” (Genesis 1:5). The holy Divine Presence is the mystical meaning of “the lesser light to rule the night” (Genesis 1:16), and it is called “fear of heaven,” for the righteous must raise feminine waters by means of their awakening from below, and [they must] rectify [ Malkhut ] with the partition that raises returning light. Then the shefa will be drawn from above to below, but in no other manner, as is known.

This is the mystical meaning of: “And God has so made it, that men should fear before Him” (Ecclesiastes 3:14). There can be no awakening from below or raising of feminine waters without fear. This is the mystical meaning of [the] rule [of the attribute of judgment] over the night. [It is] through the lack of light, which is the aspect of night and which includes all judgments and suffering, which are the opposite of the aspect of day which is Ḥesed , that there is “fear before Him.” Were it not for the fear, the attribute of the day and the morning would not be revealed.

This is the mystical meaning of: “And there was evening and there was morning, one day.” The night also infiltrates the morning, since were it not for the night there would be no morning, and it is impossible otherwise. This is the mystical meaning of: **“God** [ El ] **is furious every day,”** because the attribute of Ḥesed , which is called ** El ,** is revealed only through the night, which is the aspect of **fury.** This is why the fury is also considered Ḥesed , because the Ḥesed cannot be revealed in any other way [other than this contrast]. From this perspective, the holy Divine Presence is also called ** El **.

[The Zohar ] thus states: **“Glory of God** [ El ]” **is the glory of the bride, who is called El ,”** that is, with respect to the verse: **“God** [ El ] **is furious every day,”** which means that it is impossible for there to be day without the fury of the night. **“On all the days of the year she is called El ,”** for such is the case in the six days of creation: It is written on each of them, “and there was evening and there was morning, one day” or “a second day,” and so on and so forth. Thus, the night [in each case] falls under the name of the day. Therefore [ Malkhut ] is called ** El ,** which is the name of Ḥesed , on the six days of creation, and also during the 6, 000 years [of this world].

[The Zohar ] continues: **“But now,** [on the festival of Shavuot] etc.” At the great fusion of the completion of the rectification, the light of the moon shall be like the light of the sun, in the mystical meaning of the verse: “But it shall come to pass that at evening time there shall be light” (Zechariah 14:7). Thus, the levels [of Malkhut ] are doubled, because [it was even] during the 6, 000 years as well, that the light of the moon [which is Malkhut ] was in the mystical meaning of: “And there was evening and there was morning.” **“But now,”** when [the Malkhut ] itself has become as large as the sun, which is Ze’er Anpin called **“glory,”** [the Malkhut ] has glory on top of glory, for [the Malkhut ] has now become the essence of glory, since it has grown [to match] Ze’er Anpin .

“Glory” is translated as **honor**, which is why [the Zohar ] states **“honor on top of honor.”** The same [applies] to “double light,” because [it was also the case] during the 6, 000 years that [the Malkhut ] was incorporated in the morning light, in the mystical meaning of: “And there was evening and there was morning, one day.” But now that [the Malkhut ] has grown [to match] the sun, it becomes the essence of the light, and [the Malkhut ] then has its own **light, in addition to the light** it had from its incorporation from before [during the 6000 years of this world].

The same [can be said] with [regard to the] **“reign on top of reign.”** During the 6, 000 years [the Malkhut ] had reign, which was dominion, only with respect to “the lesser light to rule the night.” Now, however, the dominion of the day has also been added to [the Malkhut ], since it has grown [to match] the light of the sun, which is for the rule of the day. [The Zohar ] thereby teaches us that we must not erroneously think that when [the Malkhut has grown to [match] the light of the sun, the pre-existing levels [of the Malkhut ], which [the Malkhut ] had during the 6, 000 years, are nullified, Heaven forbid. This is not the case; rather, there is only an addition here to the levels [of the Malkhut ], in such a manner that it has **glory on top of glory** etc.

**130. “Then, at that time etc.” Then, at that time, when the heavens,** which is Ze’er Anpin , **enters the wedding canopy, and comes and illuminates for her, all those colleagues who established her,** through the Torah engagement during the night, **all become known by their names there. This is** the meaning of **the verse: “And the firmament says His handiwork”** (Psalms 19:2). **“His handiwork” are those who have the sign of the covenant,** who **are called “His handiwork,” as it is stated: “Establish You upon us the work of our hands,” which is** a sign of the **covenant that is imprinted upon a man’s flesh.**

Explanation: The **colleagues** are those who preserve the Torah, in which there is practice [ assiya ], which is [relating to] good and evil. The [ Zohar ] is saying that even those parts in which the aspect of evil is still without rectification are also **“known by their names”** of holiness. [The Zohar ] thus states that **“this is** [the meaning of] **the verse: And the firmament says His handiwork [ ma’aseh ],”** because the firmament is the **book of remembrance,** as explained below, which is the mystical meaning of the light of the great fusion [of the future], which brings to repentance out of love, when willful transgressions become for them like merits ( Yoma 86b). Even with regard to those who chose to slander, it will be said about them, “Then those who feared the Lord spoke with one another etc.” (Malachi 3:16, as explained above in section #126#; see there).

Thus, it is this practice [of Torah], of the preservation of the Torah in which there is good and evil, and in which it is good for one who merits and bad for one who does not merit, the whole of the practice has now ascended into a state of holiness and has become the **handiwork** of the Holy One, blessed be He. Even upon those who did not merit, **“the firmament says”** that “then those who feared the Lord spoke with one another,” as stated. Accordingly, it is [revealed] that all the colleagues performed only holy service, because they established her for the wedding canopy, and they **“all become known by their names.”**

[The Zohar ] continues: **“As it is stated: Establish You upon us the work of our hands.”** Now, this proof appears to contradict [the idea for which it was cited as evidence]. The verse states **“the work of our hands,”** not **“the work of His hands.”** However, the proof is cited from the verse only with respect to [the claim that] **the sign of the covenant** is called **“the work of our hands.”** “Establish You upon us” is the aspect of Yesod that establishes and founds the entire structure, and the rectification of the Yesod is the covenant of circumcision. Consequently, the sign of the covenant is called **“the work of our hands,”** since we remove the foreskin from the Yesod , and this is **the work of our hands.**

This is [the case] only before the completion of the rectification, but at the completion of the rectification, everything will be revealed as the **handiwork** of the Holy One, blessed be He, and He Himself will remove the foreskin. [The Zohar ] thus states that [“His handiwork”] **are those who have the sign of the covenant,** [who] **are called “His handiwork.”** For then the Holy One, blessed be He, will Himself remove the foreskin, which is the mystical meaning of: **“The firmament shows His handiwork,”** and a proof is brought regarding the rectification of the covenant, which is currently called **“the work of our hands,”** from the verse: **“Establish You upon us the work of our hands.”**

**131. “Rav Hamnuna Saba etc.” Rav Hamnuna Saba said the following: “Do not let your mouth bring your flesh into sin”** (Ecclesiastes 5:5). This means **that a person must not let his mouth** cause **the arrival of an evil thought, and** [thereby] **cause that holy flesh in which the holy covenant is inscribed to come to guilt. For if he does so, he will be drawn into Gehennom. The one appointed over Gehennom is called Duma, and several myriads of destructive angels are with him, and he stands before the entrance to Gehennom, but he has no permission to draw near to all those who protected the holy covenant in this world.**
